sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4.86 billion in FY2016 to $14.3 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].
The path was not smooth: FY2021 revenue jumped 89.1% to $16.1 billion, then fell 24.3% in FY2022 to $12.2 billion [D241][F6][D292][F7].
REGEN-COV contributed 66.4pp of growth and 36.3% of revenue in FY2021 [D582][D580], then fell to zero in FY2022 [S49].
Growth has since flattened, with revenue up 7.8%, 8.3% and 1.0% in FY2023 to FY2025 [D342][D391][D440], and the three-year revenue CAGR is 5.6% [D767].
The growth engine has rotated from EYLEA to collaboration profit shares: US EYLEA was 63.0% of revenue in FY2017 [D554] but only 19.2% in FY2025 [D576].
US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% in FY2025, which the filing attributes to competitive pressure, compounded bevacizumab, the EYLEA HD transition and a lower net selling price [D577][P10].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits contributed 9.3pp of FY2025 growth and reached 36.5% of revenue [D592][D590], while collaboration revenue overall was 51.1% of revenue [D521].
That profit share rose 33.6% in FY2025, driven by higher Dupixent sales [D591][P9].
Operating income grew slower than revenue over the window, at an 11.6% CAGR against 12.8% [F199][F198], and fell 10.3% in FY2025 [D441].
The FY2025 operating margin of 24.9% is the window low, 9.7pp below the 34.6% median and 30.8pp below the FY2021 high of 55.7% [F30][D749][D751][D750].
The margin fell 3.2pp in FY2025, with R&D costing 4.7pp and SG&A adding back 2.0pp [D453][D465][D466].
R&D reached 40.8% of revenue in FY2025, far above the 20.1% biopharma peer median [D420][D779].
SG&A fell 8.6% on lower charitable contributions to the Good Days patient assistance fund [D456][P5].
Net margin held at 31.4% because other income of $1.65 billion lifted net margin 6.5pp above operating margin [F50][X117][D797].
Operating cash flow of $4.98 billion was 1.11x net income in FY2025, in line with the 1.10x window median [F80][F40][D428][D787].
Free cash flow of $4.08 billion was 0.91x net income and a 28.4% margin, above the 26.4% window median [F100][D429][D425][D757].
Capex rose 18.9% to $898 million, 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [D447][F90][D424][D430].
Stock-based compensation of $994 million equalled 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431].
Net cash reached $16.9 billion, 117.7% of revenue, the 100th percentile against eight biopharma peers whose median is net debt of 50.7% of revenue [D434][D435][D780][D781].
Debt is a flat $1.99 billion of senior notes [F187], and the current ratio is 4.13x against a 3.97x window median [F180][D766].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3.81 billion consumed 93.3% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D436][D437], and the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D459].
A first dividend of $370 million was paid in FY2025 [X140], while acquisitions were negligible at $3.3 million [X145].
Operating margin has fallen four years running, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F30][R1].
The decline is structural: EYLEA is shrinking on competition and the HD transition [P10], while R&D intensity keeps climbing [D420].
The revenue basis is inconsistent: FY2018 is shown as $5.15 billion against $6.71 billion first reported, and FY2019 as $6.56 billion against $7.86 billion [F3][X3][F4][X4][R2].
That recast makes the FY2018 revenue decline of 12.4% and the FY2019 rebound of 27.4% unreliable as reported [D92][D143][R2].
Watch whether the operating margin holds above the FY2025 low of 24.9% [F30][D749]; a further decline would extend the four-year slide [R1].
Watch US EYLEA sales against the FY2025 level of $2.75 billion [S43]; stabilization would signal the HD transition is absorbing the erosion [P10][P11].
Watch R&D as a share of revenue against the FY2025 40.8% [D420]; a move back toward the 34.6% window median would restore operating leverage [D760].
